key_insight: This paper studies when calibration actually helps mixture-of-experts models, especially under distribution shift. The main takeaway is that calibrating individual experts can improve MoE behavior, but the benefit depends on how the data distribution changes and how experts are routed.
problem_solved: Mixture-of-experts models often perform well empirically, but it is unclear when enforcing calibration on each expert improves prediction quality and uncertainty estimates, especially when test data differs from training data.
method: Analyze calibration at the level of individual experts rather than only the final ensemble output.
Study mixture-of-experts behavior under distribution shift to identify when calibrated experts lead to better uncertainty estimates and performance.
Compare calibrated versus uncalibrated expert predictions to understand the conditions where calibration is beneficial.
impact: For practitioners, this helps make MoE systems more trustworthy by clarifying when calibration will improve reliability. It can guide model design and deployment in settings where data drift or shift is expected, such as healthcare, robotics, and large-scale decision systems.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram of MoE routing with multiple experts and a gating network.
A before/after chart comparing calibration error under in-distribution vs shifted data.
An uncertainty diagram showing predicted probabilities versus empirical outcomes.
An icon set representing experts, routing, distribution shift, and calibration.
paper_title: Toward Calibrated Mixture-of-Experts Under Distribution Shift
paper_authors: Gina Wong, Drew Prinster, Suchi Saria, Rama Chellappa, Anqi Liu
